All correct. Here's the summary for this round:

**`GenericUtils.java`** — Ten casts removed in two `replace_all` passes. All nine `safeGet*` utility methods shared the identical `if (column instanceof Number) { ... ((Number) column).intValue() ... }` pattern — each method resolves a column to either an integer index or a string name, dispatching to a JDBC overload. Binding variable `n` at the `instanceof Number n` check eliminates the cast in every branch. A tenth cast on `isLegacySQLDialect` (`((GenericSQLDialect) dialect).isLegacySQLDialect()`) was also converted to a guarded pattern `dialect instanceof GenericSQLDialect gsd && gsd.isLegacySQLDialect()`.

**`DateTimeDataFormatter.java`** — Five casts in `formatValue` replaced with pattern bindings. The outermost `instanceof TemporalAccessor` check now binds `ta`, so the final `return dateTimeFormatter.format((TemporalAccessor) value)` becomes `format(ta)`. Each nested type check (`LocalDateTime`, `ZonedDateTime`, `OffsetDateTime`) also binds its variable, so `.atZone()`, `.withZoneSameInstant()`, and `.atZoneSameInstant()` calls no longer need casts. The `instanceof Date` check additionally uses a guarded pattern (`instanceof Date d && zone != null`) to fold the condition into the existing `null` check.

**`SimplePreferenceStore.java`** — The `equals` guard used the early-return negated pattern (`if (!(obj instanceof T))`) followed by an explicit cast one line later. Java's negated pattern binding (`if (!(obj instanceof SimplePreferenceStore copy))`) places `copy` in scope in the else branch — the explicit cast declaration is removed entirely.
